 ORDER 1 .
With the consent of the learned counsel for the parties, the appeal is finally heard.

2. This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellants / claimants being aggrieved by the award dated 10/5/2019 passed by the 4th Additional,
Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Ratlam whereby a total sum of Rs.9,88,176/- has been awarded to the appellants / claimants by way of compensation.

entities.text:
4th Additional,
Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Ratlam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Short facts of the case are that Rishabh Kumar Jain (since deceased) on 16/4/2015 in the evening was going with Scotty bearing registration No.M.P. 43 MH 6587 from village Delanpur to Sailana.

At that time the respondent No.1/driver came with Bolero car bearing registration No.M.P. 43 T 0869 driving the same from wrong side in a rash and negligent manner and dashed with the Scotty of the deceased as a result of which he fell down and sustained grievous NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:25161 2 MA-4270-2019 injuries on his head, face and ear.
He was taken to the District Hospital, Ratlam.
On account of the injuries received by Rishabh Jain, he eventually expired.
4. The appellants / claimants filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

Learned tribunal considering the evidence available on record awarded a total compensation of Rs.9,88,176/- to the appellants as well as respondent No.6.
5.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the claims tribunal erred in calculating the income of the deceased Rishabh Kumar Jain.
He points out that the claims tribunal in para 17, 18 and 19 of the award has considered the aspect of the income of the deceased.

He points out that after referring Asha Jain vs Balram on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115250306/
1 to Exhibits P/30, P/31 and P/32 income tax returns the claims tribunal recorded that in those returns income of the deceased was mentioned as Rs.1,76,600/-, Rs.1,85,560/- and Rs.1,31,438/-
and even after mentioning this, the statutory deduction of Chapter 6- A were excluded and thus as per last return of Exhibit P/32 income of the deceased was taken at Rs.1,23,660/-.

sentences.text: 6 . Learned counsel for the appellants submits that this exclusion by the claims tribunal is in complete misconception of the fact that the deduction was for some levy, infact it was an exemption from payment of tax because the deduction of Rs.7,777/- was under the Chapter 6-A of the Income Tax Act, which is a deduction providing exemption from payment of tax and this was for the reason that said amount of Rs.7,777/- was LIC payment made by the deceased.
Thus in terms of even Exhibit P/32 the income of the deceased should have been taken at Rs.1,31,438/-.
Apart from this he also points out that the appellant disclosed in his income tax return agriculture income of Rs.55,000/-.

Exhibit P/35 is the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:25161 3 MA-4270-2019 intimation issued under Section 143 of the Income Tax Act in which this amount of Rs.55,000/- has been mentioned as agriculture income.
He further points out that Exhibit P/28 is the Kistbandi Khatoni of the agriculture land of Rishabh Kumar Jain.

He thus submits that it was amply proved before the claims tribunal that apart from the return income of Rs.1,31,000/- the deceased was also earning from agriculture income, hence the claims tribunal erred in taking the income of the deceased at Rs.1,23,660/-.

Apart from this, counsel for the appellant also stated that the claims tribunal has not awarded consortium to all the claimants except the wife although other three claimants were two sons and mother of the deceased.
Thus they all were entitled for amount of consortium.

7 . Learned counsel for the appellants has also argued that the claims tribunal has erred in not saddling the State for payment of compensation because the vehicle in question was engaged by the State during the period when accident occurred.
He thus prays for enhancement of compensation and for directing State also to pay the compensation severally and jointly.
8 . Per contra, learned counsel for the State opposes the prayer.

Learned counsel for the State points out that at the time of accident the vehicle was not being used in the course of official work but it was on a private journey, thus the State cannot be made liable.
As regards the owner of the vehicle he has not appeared even after service.
Counsel for respondent No.5 submits that as there was no order against the Insurance Company hence he has nothing to say in the case.

9. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
10.

On perusal of Exhibit P/32, it is clear that the claims tribunal has erred NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:25161 4 MA-4270-2019 in deducting the amount of Rs.7777/- from the total income of the deceased Rishabh Kumar Jain.
The deduction was under Chapter 6A which was for benefit of the assessee from liability of income tax, it was not exclusion from the income.
The claims tribunal erred in understanding the impact of such deduction.
As such it is held that the income of the appellant as contained in Exhihit P/32 at Rs.1,31,438/- has to be taken as it is.
As regards the income from agricultural activity though it is true that Kistbandi Khatoni is there showing the agricultural land of the appellant.

However the fact remains that income will continue to come from Asha Jain vs Balram on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115250306/
2 the said agricultural land even after the death of Rishabh Kumar Jain.

sentences.text: However, the legal heirs may have to employee some person for supervision or performance of agricultural activity.
Keeping this in view a further addition of Rs.5000/- is made in the income of the deceased.
As such the income of the deceased is taken at Rs.1,31,438 + Rs.5000/- = Rs.1,36,438/-.
As regards the amount of consortium it is seen from para 25 that only amount of Rs.40,000/- has been awarded to the wife of the deceased for loss of consortium.

In view of the law as laid down in the case of Megma General Insurance Co.Ltd. vs. Nanu Ram (2018) 18 SCC 130, both the sons and respondent No.6 are also entitled for compensation for loss of consortium.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus all the three of them are awarded Rs.40,000/- each which totals to Rs.1,20,000/-.

As such now the payable compensation after deducting the already awarded amount of Rs.9,88,176/- will be as under :-
 Loss of Dependency Income - Rs.1,36,438/-
 Future prospects - Rs.1,36,438 X 10% = 13,643.
 1,36,438 + 13,643.8  Multiplier adopted - 1,50,081.8 X 9 = Rs.13,50,7  Consortium - 1,20,000/-
 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:25161  5   - = Rs.14,70,736.2  Consortium to wife + loss of  estate, funeral expenses - Rs.70,000/-
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 Total - Rs.15,40,736  Awarded amount by Claim Tribunal - Rs.9,88,176.

Enhanced amount by this Court = Rs.5,52,560 /-
11.
The appellants are hence entitled for payment of enhanced amount of Rs.5,52,560/- with an interest of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the application before the claims tribunal.
12. As regards the liability of the State it has clearly come on record that the offending vehicle was being used for private purposed at the time of accident.
The tribunal in para 29 of the award has recorded specific findings in this regard.
The learned counsel for the appellant has not been able to establish any perversity in such findings.
In view of the clear admission of respondents No.1 and 2 in this regard no interference is warranted in this regard.
As such the State cannot be held liable for payment of compensation.

In this view of the matter, the other terms of the award shall remain Asha Jain vs Balram on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115250306/
3 intact.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE SS/-
